key_insight: Trustworthy protein–ligand binding predictions require trustworthy evaluation. This paper advocates transparent data, code and experimental procedures, alongside safeguards against data leakage and bias.
problem_solved: Data leakage, biased benchmarks and unclear evaluation procedures can inflate apparent performance and undermine fair comparisons between structure-based binding prediction methods.
method: Advocate transparent reporting of datasets, code and experimental procedures.
Discuss good practices for preventing data leakage and bias during evaluation.
Promote fair, reproducible and meaningful comparisons across scoring methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, these guidelines help distinguish genuine predictive progress from evaluation artifacts. More rigorous benchmarking makes model comparisons more reliable.
visual_elements: Protein–ligand binding illustration showing the prediction task.
Train/test split diagram with a blocked arrow representing data leakage.
Transparency checklist with data, code and experimental-procedure icons.
Side-by-side scoring-method comparison using a shared evaluation protocol.
paper_title: Guidelines for evaluating structure-based methods for protein–ligand binding prediction
